name: Sidi Okba Mosque
scope: Standing historic Sidi Okba prayer hall, two shallow domes, minaret, attached tomb envelope and a representative short entry court. Modern complex buildings have separate scope.
era: Surviving historic core of the Sidi Okba complex, reconstructed from 1893 and circa-1900 documentation and present descriptions of the retained historic core.

originalReview.notes: The 1893 exterior close view shows the deep rendered wall, battered plaster, plain niche and low attached plastered vault and unglazed openings. Later repair state is not inferred from damage in the source.

originalReview.notes: The 1893 view documents the thick whitewashed piers, shallow imposts and unornamented arches of the roofed prayer hall.

originalReview.notes: The circa-1900 Collections ND postcard shows the square minaret, paired recessed lower panels and upper openings, projecting cornice, stepped merlons, two shallow domes and a low arcade in front of the historic core.

review.method: Exact Qualla originals of the historic standing components with native archive provenance and surveyed hall measurements
review.notes: Exact published Qualla originals are two dated French Base Mémoire photographs and a circa-1900 Collections ND postcard with the original card caption. Historic tower and dome shapes are checked against the modern written descriptions of the retained components. Attribution-conditioned current photos and the archival view with an incomplete Qualla rights record were excluded.
